newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asian Terminals to issue 1.5 bln-peso debt.
newsitem.headline: Asian Terminals to issue 1.5 bln-peso debt.

text.p: Asian Terminal Inc (ATI) plans to sell 1.5 billion pesos worth of long-term commercial papers starting this April to fund its various projects over the next 18 months, Ricard Barclay, the company's executive vice president, said on Thursday.
ATI is the sole container terminal operator for the South Harbour in Manila. It is also the sole multi-cargo operator for the port of Manila.
The company might also offer bonds after the sale of long-term commercial papers, Barclay said.

Arturo Lopez, company treasurer, said they may offer the long-term papers in four tranches in a span of every three months. It may carry a maturity of three to six years, with the interest based on the 91-day T-bill rate.
He added the company decided on this option to reduce its foreign exchange risk with its exposure to foreign debt.

The company had programmed a capital budget of one billion pesos every year. Its current projects include leasehold improvements and equipment acquisition at the South Harbor; an inland clearance depot and logistics center in Calamba, Laguna south of Manila; and the expansion of its bulk grains terminal.
Barclay also told analysts the company is looking at other port development projects, such as the Batangas port, Subic free port and other major cities around the country.
He said the company had forecast a net profit of 350 million pesos in the current fiscal year ending June 1997, a 25 percent rise from 279 million pesos in the previous year.
Revenues this year could grow by 74 percent to 2.652 billion pesos from 1.527 billion pesos.
Net profits could further rise by 27 percent to 445 million pesos in the fiscal year ending June 1998 on revenues of 3.089 billion pesos, he said.
The earnings projections assume a 10 to 20 percent volume growth, increases in tariffs it can charge customers, and an average yearly inflation rate of 10 percent, he said.
ATI's market share in foreign container trade in Manila was at 37 percent at the end of 1996, equivalent to 480,000 twenty equivalent units (TEUs), from 36 percent in 1995.
